# tidystata

[tidystata](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/) is a set of functions
that combines Stata-inspired features with tidyverse-style operations.

The package focuses on exploring and preparing data:

- [`tab()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md),
  [`tab1()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md), and
  [`tab2()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md) for
  frequency tables.
- [`fre()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md),
  [`fre1()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md), and
  [`fre2()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md) for
  frequency tables with totals.
- [`summ()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/summ.md) and
  [`tabstat()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/summ.md)
  for summary statistics.
- [`pwcorr()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/pwcorr.md),
  [`misstable()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/misstable.md),
  and `tab2(.chi2 = TRUE)` for correlations, missing values, and tests
  of independence.
- [`codebook()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/codebook.md)
  and
  [`variables()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/variables.md)
  for variable inspection.
- [`isid()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/keys.md),
  [`duplicates_report()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/keys.md),
  [`assert()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/assert.md),
  [`is_first()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/is_first.md),
  and
  [`s_merge()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/s_merge.md)
  for checking keys and merging, and
  [`print_all()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/special-print.md)
  for listing every row.
- [`s_select()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/s_select.md),
  row calculations, conversion helpers,
  [`std()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/std.md),
  [`pc()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/std.md),
  [`as_dummy()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/as_dummy.md),
  panel lags
  ([`s_lag()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/panel.md),
  [`s_lead()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/panel.md),
  [`s_diff()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/panel.md)),
  and binning for data preparation.

tidystata `0.3.0` retires the import/export, regression-table, and
detailed-codebook wrappers. See the [migration
guide](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/articles/migration.html) for
direct package alternatives and breaking changes. This experimental
package is undergoing stabilization; see
[NEWS](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/news/index.html) for changes
in each release.

## Installation

You can install the development version of tidystata like so:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("socimh/tidystata")
```

R 4.1.0 or later and a suitable build toolchain are required to install
from source. Rich table formatting is optional and requires `flextable`.

If you already have this source repository on your computer, open
`tidystata.Rproj` and restart R before installing the local changes:

``` r

devtools::install(".", upgrade = "never", build_vignettes = FALSE)
```

Restart R again, then check the version and installed location:

``` r

library(tidystata)
packageVersion("tidystata")
find.package("tidystata")
```

Opening the source folder alone does not change what
[`library(tidystata)`](https://github.com/socimh/tidystata) loads.
Repeat the installation after editing source code. During package
development, `devtools::load_all(".")` loads the working source into the
current session; installation followed by a fresh R session tests the
installed package.

## Learn the workflow

Read [Getting
started](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/articles/getting-started.html)
for a small exploration and preparation workflow, and [Containers and
missing
values](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/articles/containers-and-missing-values.html)
for return types, grouping, labels and previews. In an installation that
includes vignettes, use
[`vignette("getting-started", package = "tidystata")`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/articles/getting-started.md).

Coming from Stata?
[`findit()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/findit.md)
gives the R equivalent of a Stata command. Type one Stata word bare, or
quote anything longer; the usual Stata abbreviations work:

``` r

findit(reg)
findit("merge 1:1 id, keep(match)")
findit(left_join) # R functions work too
```

The [Coming from
Stata](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/articles/coming-from-stata.html)
article lists every entry by topic, in English and
[Chinese](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/articles/coming-from-stata-zh.html),
including the packages to use beyond tidystata.

Plain manual scripts are in the source repository’s
[`examples/`](https://github.com/socimh/tidystata/tree/master/examples)
folder. Open a script in your editor and run its lines individually;
from a source checkout,
`source("examples/02_frequency_tables.R", echo = TRUE)` runs a complete
example. The full [migration
guide](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/articles/migration.html) is on
the website.

## Table return types

Most table-producing helpers, including the `tab`, `summ`, `codebook`
and `variables` families, preserve the input container by default: a
tibble returns a tibble, a base data frame returns a base data frame,
and a data.table returns a data.table. List outputs remain lists, with
each table following the same rule. Explicit output options override
this default.
[`pwcorr()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/pwcorr.md),
[`misstable()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/misstable.md)
and
[`duplicates_report()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/keys.md)
always return tibbles, as their help pages state. Summaries and variable
inventories are ungrouped; grouping columns are retained where the
function normally reports them. Arbitrary data-frame subclass metadata
is not guaranteed on newly constructed tables. Vector and scalar helpers
retain their usual outputs.

[`preview_table()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/special-print.md)
preserves the underlying container while changing its console display.
[`unpreview_table()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/special-print.md)
removes that display setting. External dplyr and tidyr verbs retain
their own container and grouping behavior, with preview settings
preserved for supported operations.

## Example

### Load the package

Load `tidystata` and the data-manipulation package used in these
examples.

``` r

library(tidystata)
library(dplyr)
```

### codebook()

View the codebook of `lifeexp`.

``` r

codebook(lifeexp)
#> # A tibble: 6 x 5
#>   variable  label                    type             n unique
#>   <chr>     <chr>                    <chr>        <int>  <int>
#> 1 region    Region                   double+label    68      3
#> 2 country   Country                  character       68     68
#> 3 popgrowth Avg. annual % growth     double          68     32
#> 4 lexp      Life expectancy at birth double          68     20
#> 5 gnppc     GNP per capita           double          67     64
#> 6 safewater Safe water               double          54     32
```

### summ()

Summarise selected numeric variables in `mtcars`.

``` r

summ(mtcars, mpg, wt)
#>   name type  n unique    min     mean        sd    max
#> 1  mpg  dbl 32     25 10.400 20.09062 6.0269481 33.900
#> 2   wt  dbl 32     29  1.513  3.21725 0.9784574  5.424
```

Choose numeric variables deliberately: means and standard deviations of
factor codes may have no substantive interpretation. Numeric and logical
columns with no observed values are retained: `n` and `unique` are zero
and summary statistics are `NA`, including `sum`.

Select statistics with `.stat`. Aliases `missing`, `p25`, `p50`, and
`p75` retain their requested names and order; `sum` is available for
numeric summaries. Unsupported statistics produce an error. See the
[migration
guide](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/articles/migration.html) for
the date/datetime restrictions and cross-tabulation naming rules.

``` r

summ(mtcars, mpg, .stat = c("missing", "p50", "sum"))
#>   type missing  p50   sum
#> 1  dbl       0 19.2 642.9
```

With `.type = "table"`, numeric and calendar summaries share character
columns for formatted statistics; counts remain numeric. Default list
mode preserves numeric statistic types in the numeric summary.

### tab()

Tabulate a single variable:

``` r

tab(dplyr::starwars, sex)
#> # A tibble: 5 x 6
#>   sex                n percent   cum valid valid_cum
#>   <chr>          <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 female            16   18.4   18.4 19.3       19.3
#> 2 hermaphroditic     1    1.15  19.5  1.20      20.5
#> 3 male              60   69.0   88.5 72.3       92.8
#> 4 none               6    6.90  95.4  7.23     100  
#> 5 <NA>               4    4.60 100   NA         NA
```

[`tab1()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md)
tabulates variables one by one as a list, and
[`varlist()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/varlist.md)
can select variables in a Stata style.

``` r

tab1(dplyr::starwars, varlist("*color"))
#> $hair_color
#> # A tibble: 12 x 6
#>    value             n percent    cum valid valid_cum
#>    <chr>         <int>   <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 auburn            1    1.15   1.15  1.22      1.22
#>  2 auburn, grey      1    1.15   2.30  1.22      2.44
#>  3 auburn, white     1    1.15   3.45  1.22      3.66
#>  4 black            13   14.9   18.4  15.9      19.5 
#>  5 blond             3    3.45  21.8   3.66     23.2 
#>  6 blonde            1    1.15  23.0   1.22     24.4 
#>  7 brown            18   20.7   43.7  22.0      46.3 
#>  8 brown, grey       1    1.15  44.8   1.22     47.6 
#>  9 grey              1    1.15  46.0   1.22     48.8 
#> 10 none             38   43.7   89.7  46.3      95.1 
#> 11 white             4    4.60  94.3   4.88    100   
#> 12 <NA>              5    5.75 100    NA        NA   
#> 
#> $skin_color
#> # A tibble: 31 x 6
#>    value                   n percent   cum valid valid_cum
#>    <chr>               <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 blue                    2    2.30  2.30  2.30      2.30
#>  2 blue, grey              2    2.30  4.60  2.30      4.60
#>  3 brown                   4    4.60  9.20  4.60      9.20
#>  4 brown mottle            1    1.15 10.3   1.15     10.3 
#>  5 brown, white            1    1.15 11.5   1.15     11.5 
#>  6 dark                    6    6.90 18.4   6.90     18.4 
#>  7 fair                   17   19.5  37.9  19.5      37.9 
#>  8 fair, green, yellow     1    1.15 39.1   1.15     39.1 
#>  9 gold                    1    1.15 40.2   1.15     40.2 
#> 10 green                   6    6.90 47.1   6.90     47.1 
#> # i 21 more rows
#> 
#> $eye_color
#> # A tibble: 15 x 6
#>    value             n percent   cum valid valid_cum
#>    <chr>         <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 black            10   11.5   11.5 11.5       11.5
#>  2 blue             19   21.8   33.3 21.8       33.3
#>  3 blue-gray         1    1.15  34.5  1.15      34.5
#>  4 brown            21   24.1   58.6 24.1       58.6
#>  5 dark              1    1.15  59.8  1.15      59.8
#>  6 gold              1    1.15  60.9  1.15      60.9
#>  7 green, yellow     1    1.15  62.1  1.15      62.1
#>  8 hazel             3    3.45  65.5  3.45      65.5
#>  9 orange            8    9.20  74.7  9.20      74.7
#> 10 pink              1    1.15  75.9  1.15      75.9
#> 11 red               5    5.75  81.6  5.75      81.6
#> 12 red, blue         1    1.15  82.8  1.15      82.8
#> 13 unknown           3    3.45  86.2  3.45      86.2
#> 14 white             1    1.15  87.4  1.15      87.4
#> 15 yellow           11   12.6  100   12.6      100
```

One-way tabulation also counts list-column values. Selecting no
variables returns an empty result;
[`tab1()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md) and
[`fre1()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md) return
empty lists by default. Matrix columns are unsupported.

[`tab2()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md)
cross-tabulates two variables.

``` r

tab2(dplyr::starwars, sex, gender)
#> # A tibble: 5 x 4
#>   `sex \\ gender` feminine masculine  `NA`
#>   <chr>              <int>     <int> <int>
#> 1 female                16         0     0
#> 2 hermaphroditic         0         1     0
#> 3 male                   0        60     0
#> 4 none                   1         5     0
#> 5 <NA>                   0         0     4
```

### fre()

[`fre()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md) family
functions simply add total rows (and total columns in
[`fre2()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md)) to
their [`tab()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md)
counterparts.

[`fre()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md) and
[`fre2()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md) default
to `.type = "auto"`, preserving the input container.
[`fre1()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md) returns
a list whose tables preserve that container. Request `.type = "tibble"`
explicitly when a tibble is required.

``` r

fre(dplyr::starwars, sex)
#> # A tibble: 7 x 6
#>   sex                n percent   cum  valid valid_cum
#>   <chr>          <int>   <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 female            16   18.4   18.4  19.3       19.3
#> 2 hermaphroditic     1    1.15  19.5   1.20      20.5
#> 3 male              60   69.0   88.5  72.3       92.8
#> 4 none               6    6.90  95.4   7.23     100  
#> 5 Valid Total       83   95.4   NA   100         NA  
#> 6 <NA>               4    4.60 100    NA         NA  
#> 7 Total             87  100     NA    NA         NA
```

For optional rich formatting, install `flextable` and request it
explicitly:

``` r

fre(dplyr::starwars, sex, .type = "flextable")
```

### Row calculations and binning

Row helpers return vectors that can be used in
[`mutate()`](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/mutate.html):

``` r

tibble(a = c(1, NA, 3), b = c(3, NA, 5)) |>
  mutate(row_average = row_mean(a, b))
#> # A tibble: 3 x 3
#>       a     b row_average
#>   <dbl> <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1     1     3           2
#> 2    NA    NA          NA
#> 3     3     5           4
```

[`xtile()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/cut.md) keeps
equal values in the same group. Ties can reduce the number of intervals,
with a warning, rather than splitting equal values by row order.

# Package index

## Coming from Stata

- [`findit()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/findit.md) :
  Find the R equivalent of a Stata command

## Inspect variables

- [`browse()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/browse.md) :

  Browse columns like Stata's `browse` command

- [`codebook()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/codebook.md)
  : View the codebook of a dataset or selected columns

- [`misstable()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/misstable.md)
  : Tabulate missing values

- [`ds()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/names.md)
  [`ds_as_column()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/names.md)
  [`names_as_column()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/names.md)
  : List column names by tidyselect

- [`var_type()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/var_type.md)
  [`var_unit()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/var_type.md)
  : Report an object's type or unit

- [`variables()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/variables.md)
  [`variables_search()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/variables.md)
  : Show the variable list of a dataset

## Tabulate

- [`pwcorr()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/pwcorr.md) :
  Pairwise correlations
- [`tab()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md)
  [`tab1()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md)
  [`tab2()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md)
  [`xtab()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md)
  [`fre2()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md)
  [`fre()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md)
  [`fre1()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/tab.md) :
  Tabulate columns

## Summarise

- [`summ()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/summ.md)
  [`tabstat()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/summ.md) :
  Summarise columns

## Check and combine data

- [`assert()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/assert.md) :
  Assert that conditions hold
- [`is_first()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/is_first.md)
  [`s_tag()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/is_first.md)
  : Flag the first row of each group
- [`isid()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/keys.md)
  [`duplicates_report()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/keys.md)
  [`duplicates_tag()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/keys.md)
  [`duplicates_list()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/keys.md)
  [`duplicates_drop()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/keys.md)
  : Check keys and duplicate rows
- [`s_merge()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/s_merge.md)
  : Merge two tables with a Stata-style match report

## Generate variables

- [`as_dummy()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/as_dummy.md)
  [`tab_gen()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/as_dummy.md)
  : Create indicator (dummy) variables
- [`xtile()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/cut.md)
  [`cut_quantile()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/cut.md)
  [`cut_length()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/cut.md)
  [`cut_breaks()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/cut.md)
  : Cut a numeric vector into groups
- [`s_lag()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/panel.md)
  [`s_lead()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/panel.md)
  [`s_diff()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/panel.md) :
  Panel lags, leads and differences
- [`row_mean()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/row_egen.md)
  [`row_sum()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/row_egen.md)
  [`row_max()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/row_egen.md)
  [`row_min()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/row_egen.md)
  [`row_median()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/row_egen.md)
  [`row_var()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/row_egen.md)
  [`row_sd()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/row_egen.md)
  [`row_unique()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/row_egen.md)
  [`row_nvals()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/row_egen.md)
  [`row_miss()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/row_egen.md)
  [`row_non_miss()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/row_egen.md)
  : Calculate summaries across columns within each row
- [`std()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/std.md)
  [`pc()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/std.md)
  [`pct()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/std.md) :
  Standardise a variable or scale it to a percentage

## Convert types

- [`mvdecode()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/na_conversion.md)
  [`mvencode()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/na_conversion.md)
  [`na_if_value()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/na_conversion.md)
  [`value_if_na()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/na_conversion.md)
  : Replace values with missing values or fill missing values
- [`destring()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/type_conversion.md)
  [`decode()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/type_conversion.md)
  [`tostring()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/type_conversion.md)
  [`as_character()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/type_conversion.md)
  [`as_numeric()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/type_conversion.md)
  : Convert vectors for data preparation

## Select and preview

- [`s_select()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/s_select.md)
  : Select and compute columns
- [`preview_table()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/special-print.md)
  [`unpreview_table()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/special-print.md)
  [`print_headtail()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/special-print.md)
  [`s_print()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/special-print.md)
  [`print_all()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/special-print.md)
  [`print_interval()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/special-print.md)
  [`slice_headtail()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/special-print.md)
  [`slice_interval()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/special-print.md)
  : Persistent previews of complete tables
- [`varlist()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/varlist.md)
  : Select columns with a Stata varlist

## Small tools

- [`capture()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/capture.md)
  [`s_try()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/capture.md) :
  Capture an error and report success
- [`set_seed()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/set_seed.md)
  : Set the random seed, in a pipeline or alone
- [`timer()`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/timer.md) :
  Time spent on a function
- [`` `%>%` ``](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/pipe.md) :
  Pipe operator

## Sample Data

- [`lifeexp`](https://socimh.github.io/tidystata/reference/lifeexp.md) :
  Life expectancy data in 1998
